property_summary: For any caller and any provided _unlockTime, the reference contract ensures Acc[caller].unlockTime >= block.timestamp after Put(...) (it clamps upward to now); the mutant that assigns acc.unlockTime = _unlockTime can set it < block.timestamp, violating that rule for some fuzzed inputs.

For any caller and any payable call to Put(_unlockTime), the reference contract ensures Acc[caller].unlockTime >= block.timestamp (it never sets unlockTime in the past); the mutant that assigns unlockTime = _unlockTime can make Acc[caller].unlockTime < block.timestamp for some fuzzed _unlockTime, violating this property.

After any call to Put(_unlockTime) by any caller with any msg.value, the reference contract guarantees Acc[caller].unlockTime >= block.timestamp (it clamps to now), whereas the mutant can set Acc[caller].unlockTime < block.timestamp when given a past _unlockTime.

For every caller and any call to Put(_unlockTime), the reference contract guarantees Acc[caller].unlockTime >= block.timestamp (it clamps to now); the mutant that assigns acc.unlockTime = _unlockTime can set it < block.timestamp for some fuzzed _unlockTime, violating this rule.

For every caller and any call to Put(_unlockTime) the reference contract ensures Acc[caller].unlockTime >= block.timestamp after the call (it never sets unlockTime to a past timestamp); the mutant that assigns unlockTime = _unlockTime can violate this by setting unlockTime < block.timestamp for some fuzzed _unlockTime.

Rule: calling Put(x) sets Acc[msg.sender].unlockTime to at least block.timestamp (i.e., unlockTime >= block.timestamp) in the reference for all inputs; the mutant that treats x as a duration (block.timestamp + x) can set unlockTime < block.timestamp for inputs where x is a very small value and block.timestamp has advanced between calls (or if x is 0 the reference sets unlockTime == block.timestamp while mutant may set same or larger) — specifically the general safe rule is that after Put, unlockTime is never LESS than the current block.timestamp; the mutant can violate intended absolute-time semantics by interpreting the parameter as a duration and thus produce inconsistent/earlier-than-expected unlocking behaviour for some inputs.

After calling Put(_unlockTime) from any sender with any payable value, the reference contract sets Acc[sender].unlockTime to be >= the block timestamp at the time of the call (i.e. never in the past); the mutant that treats the argument as a duration (block.timestamp + _unlockTime) can produce an unlockTime that is less than the current block timestamp for some sequences of calls/input, breaking this invariant.

For any sender and any _unlockTime passed to Put, the reference contract sets Acc[sender].unlockTime to be at least the block.timestamp observed during the Put call; the mutant that treats _unlockTime as a duration (block.timestamp + _unlockTime) can make this invariant false for some inputs (e.g., when _unlockTime is a very large value that overflows uint or when interactions produce an earlier-than-expected value), so the property detects the behavioral difference.

For any caller and any _unlockTime, after calling Put(...) the reference C stores Acc[msg.sender].unlockTime equal to max(_unlockTime, block.timestamp) (i.e. not less than the block timestamp at call time); the mutant that treats _unlockTime as a duration (adds block.timestamp) can make Acc[msg.sender].unlockTime be greater than it should for some inputs, so comparing the stored unlockTime against the expected max detects the mutant.

For every caller and any _unlockTime value, calling Put(_unlockTime) results in Acc[caller].unlockTime being equal to the maximum of the provided _unlockTime and the block.timestamp observed by Put (i.e., stored unlockTime >= block.timestamp and equals _unlockTime when _unlockTime >= block.timestamp); the mutant that treats the argument as a duration (adds block.timestamp) will make the stored unlockTime differ (be larger than expected) for some inputs.

For any caller and any provided _unlockTime, calling Put(...) on the correct contract always sets Acc[msg.sender].unlockTime to max(_unlockTime, block.timestamp); the mutant that omits the assignment can leave unlockTime unchanged (breaking this rule) for some inputs.

For any caller and any _unlockTime, after Put(...) completes the contract's Acc[msg].unlockTime is >= block.timestamp and equals max(_unlockTime, block.timestamp); the mutant that omits updating unlockTime can leave Acc[msg].unlockTime unchanged (i.e. < max(_unlockTime, block.timestamp)) for some inputs.

For any caller and any Put(_unlockTime) call, the contract sets Acc[caller].unlockTime to at least block.timestamp and specifically to max(_unlockTime, block.timestamp); the mutant that removes the assignment can leave unlockTime unchanged (below that max) for some inputs.

For any caller and any Put(_unlockTime) call, the contract sets Acc[caller].unlockTime to a value >= block.timestamp (i.e., non-decreasing to at least current time); the mutant that omits the assignment can leave Acc[caller].unlockTime unchanged below block.timestamp for some inputs, violating this invariant.

After calling Put(...) with a msg.value >= 1 wei, the reference always sets Acc[caller].unlockTime to either block.timestamp or _unlockTime whichever is greater (thus >= block.timestamp); the mutant that omits the assignment can leave unlockTime unchanged when the account had a prior unlockTime < block.timestamp, so there exist inputs where the mutant's Acc[caller].unlockTime is less than block.timestamp while the reference's is >= block.timestamp.

For any caller and any deposit value, after calling Put(...) the stored unlockTime for that caller is guaranteed to be >= the block.timestamp at which Put returned; the mutant sets unlockTime == block.timestamp (still >=) but breaks the rule that when a caller supplies a future _unlockTime > block.timestamp the stored unlockTime equals that supplied future time (i.e., Put preserves a supplied future unlockTime), which the mutant violates for some inputs.

For any caller and any deposit value, if the caller calls Put with an _unlockTime strictly in the future (> block.timestamp), then after Put returns the stored Acc[msg.sender].unlockTime equals the supplied _unlockTime; the mutant that always sets unlockTime = block.timestamp breaks this for some future _unlockTime inputs.

For any caller and any deposit, if Put is called with an _unlockTime strictly in the future (> block.timestamp) then after Put returns the stored Acc[msg.sender].unlockTime is >= block.timestamp (i.e. not in the past) and in the reference it equals the supplied future _unlockTime, whereas the mutant that always writes block.timestamp will set it to block.timestamp and thus violate equality with the supplied future value for some inputs.

For any caller and any deposit amount, if Put is called with _unlockTime strictly greater than the current block.timestamp, then after Put returns the stored Acc[msg.sender].unlockTime equals the supplied _unlockTime; the mutant that always writes block.timestamp breaks this for some future _unlockTime inputs.

For any caller and any payable deposit where the caller supplies a nonzero future _unlockTime (> block.timestamp), the reference contract stores Acc[msg.sender].unlockTime equal to that supplied value after Put returns; the mutant that always sets unlockTime = block.timestamp violates this (for some future _unlockTime inputs).

General rule: calling Put(x) never decreases the caller's unlockTime (it sets unlockTime to max(previous, provided)); the reference always ensures unlockTime >= prior unlockTime, while the mutant that sets unlockTime = _unlockTime (or uses provided value regardless) can shorten the lock for some inputs and thus violates this invariant.

For any caller and any Put call, the reference contract never decreases that caller's unlockTime (new unlockTime >= previous unlockTime); the mutant that sets unlockTime to the provided _unlockTime can shorten the lock for some inputs and thus violates this invariant.

After any Put call, the caller's unlockTime is at least its previous value (reference preserves/never decreases unlockTime); the mutant that overwrites with the provided value can decrease unlockTime for some inputs, violating this invariant.

For any caller and any Put call, the reference contract never decreases that caller's unlockTime (new unlockTime >= prior unlockTime); the mutant that sets unlockTime to the provided _unlockTime can shorten the lock for some inputs, violating this invariant.

Invariant: calling Put(...) never decreases the caller's unlockTime (new unlockTime >= previous unlockTime); the mutant that unconditionally sets unlockTime = _unlockTime can shorten it for some inputs and thus violates this rule.

property_summary: Calling Collect at a timestamp equal to the stored unlockTime does not revert (i.e. original contract allows Collect only after unlockTime, so attempting Collect when block.timestamp == acc.unlockTime in the mutant may revert), therefore for any amount and caller that previously had a deposit and unlockTime equal to current block timestamp, Collect should NOT succeed in the mutated version — we assert that if Collect reverts then the provided amount must be greater than the contract's recorded MinSum or caller balance constraints.

If a caller's recorded unlockTime equals the current block timestamp and they satisfy MinSum and requested amount, Collect succeeds (does not revert) in the original contract but fails in the mutant; so for any caller and amount where caller had previously deposited and acc.unlockTime == block.timestamp and acc.balance >= MinSum and acc.balance >= amount, Collect must not revert.

If the caller's recorded unlockTime is strictly less than the current block timestamp and their balance and MinSum conditions hold, Collect must not revert (original allows only strictly greater timestamps).
If the call is made strictly after the stored unlockTime (i.e. at a later timestamp), then Collect must not revert (Collect should succeed).

For any caller, Collect(amount) is allowed only if block.timestamp > account.unlockTime (strictly greater); the mutant allowing block.timestamp >= unlockTime lets a caller withdraw at the exact unlock timestamp, violating the strict-after rule.

For every admissible input, the reference contract only allows Collect(...) to succeed when block.timestamp is strictly greater than the account's unlockTime; the mutant that changes the check to >= can succeed at the exact unlockTime and thus violates this strict-after rule.

For every admissible input, the reference contract only allows a successful Collect when block.timestamp is strictly greater than the account's unlockTime; the mutant that uses >= can allow Collect to succeed exactly at unlockTime, violating this strict-after rule.

For all admissible inputs, the reference contract C only allows Collect(...) to succeed when block.timestamp is strictly greater than the account's unlockTime; the mutant allowing block.timestamp >= acc.unlockTime can succeed exactly at unlockTime, violating that strict-after rule.
